title: A connected eight-vertex counterexample to strict increase of outer-connected domination under the middle-graph operation
exact_endpoint: R139.MiddleOCD.mathdb_355217_connected : ¬ ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), G.Connected → 2 ≤ Fintype.card V → ocd G < ocd (middle G), and mathdb_355217_connected' for the other empty-complement convention; with g8_value, g8_value', middle_g8_value, middle_g8_value' (IsLeast value 4). The connected negation implies the negation of the literal statement.
scope: Kazemnejad, Pahlavsay, Palezzato and Torielli, arXiv:2206.15439, Conjecture 7.1 (γ̃c(G) < γ̃c(M(G)) for every graph of order n >= 2). False already for connected graphs: G8 (8 vertices, 11 edges) has γ̃c(G8) = 4 = γ̃c(M(G8)) under both conventions. Credit only for the connected negation; the edgeless failure is a domain artefact.
fidelity_review: middle-fidelity-r1/REVIEW.md (A-D PASS, E QUALIFIED_PASS; no Lean fixes)
substantive_reason: It refutes a human-posed conjecture with an explicit connected counterexample whose decisive lower bound γ̃c(G8) >= 4 uses no source ingredient; G8 is the unique connected counterexample through order 8, and the paper adds an infinite equality family and a perfect-matching characterisation of γ̃c(M(G)) = n/2. Significance is modest: the source is arXiv-only and uncited, contains errors of its own, and G8 is a small design step from its friendship graphs.
novelty_standard: Qualified bounded comparison; not worldwide priority
remaining_literature_limits: Google Scholar, MathSciNet and zbMATH not consulted
trust_limits: uniqueness at order 8, the family check and the characterisation are ordinary mathematics or computation, not Lean claims
not_claimed: Credit for the edgeless domain failure
